content:
Samuel Achterberg-Osei
Cloud Infrastructure Engineer | Azure & Terraform
Rotterdam, Netherlands | samuel.ao@example.com | +31 6 5555 0707

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud and infrastructure engineer with hands-on experience designing, building and operating Azure environments. Skilled in Terraform, infrastructure automation, cloud networking, Azure DevOps pipelines and Windows/Linux administration. Experience includes supporting a large Azure estate, operating AKS, leading a 60-server VMware-to-Azure migration, and improving deployment frequency for internal applications.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud infrastructure: Microsoft Azure, Azure VMs, VNets, Azure Firewall, private endpoints, Azure Monitor, Azure App Service, Azure Migrate
Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform, Bicep, PowerShell, Bash, Terraform module testing with Terratest
Networking and security: Hub-spoke networking, VNet peering, private DNS, TCP/IP, DNS, VPN, firewalls, MFA, conditional access
Platforms and operations: Windows Server, Linux (Ubuntu, RHEL), Kubernetes (AKS), Docker, Helm, Ansible, Active Directory, Microsoft 365 administration
CI/CD and monitoring: Azure DevOps YAML pipelines, Azure Monitor, drift detection

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Cloud Engineer (Contract) | Havenstad Logistics B.V., Rotterdam
Mar 2025 – Present
- Work in a three-person cloud team operating the company’s Azure estate of approximately 400 VMs and 12 AKS clusters across three subscriptions.
- Developed Terraform modules for hub-spoke landing zone networking, including Azure Firewall, private endpoints and connectivity across subscriptions.
- Operate AKS clusters, including upgrades, node pools and ingress; application manifests are owned by development teams.
- Replaced manual releases for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps YAML pipelines, covering build, test and deployment to App Service or AKS.
- Helped increase deployment frequency for most applications from roughly monthly to several times per week.
- Added Terratest module tests to the pipeline and a nightly infrastructure drift-detection job.

Freelance IT Administrator | Self-employed, small businesses
Sep 2022 – Jan 2024
- Set up and supported Microsoft 365 and Azure AD for nine small businesses with 5–40 employees.
- Migrated two clients from on-premises file servers to SharePoint and OneDrive.
- Created a repeatable PowerShell script and checklist for MFA, conditional access, mailbox auditing and backups.

Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services, Schiedam
Jan 2014 – Feb 2020
- Administered approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers supporting municipal services.
- Led the planning and execution of a lift-and-shift migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate; cutovers took place over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.
- Automated user provisioning and patch reporting with PowerShell.
- Provided second-line escalation for network and Active Directory issues.

Helpdesk Technician | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services
Aug 2011 – Dec 2013

CAREER BREAKS & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Mar 2020 – Aug 2022 | Full-time family caregiving; maintained Azure Administrator knowledge and provided unpaid IT support to church and family.
Feb 2024 – Feb 2025 | Studied Terraform and built a Proxmox homelab; completed a three-month, part-time online cloud bootcamp in English in Dec 2024.

EDUCATION
MBO 4, IT Systems and Networks | Delta Vocational College, 2011

CERTIFICATIONS
Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104), 2019
HashiCorp Certified: Terraform Associate (003), 2025

LANGUAGES
Dutch (native) | English (fluent) | Twi (spoken)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear section headings, a concise professional summary, relevant technical skills, quantified infrastructure scope, and measurable outcomes. The experience section presents credible progression from systems administration to cloud engineering. The 400-VM/12-AKS-cluster environment, 60-server migration, 15 application pipelines, and deployment-frequency improvement provide useful evidence of scale and impact. The career breaks are explained professionally and transparently. The document is appropriately focused on cloud infrastructure rather than general IT support. The main content limitation is that systems architecture, technical leadership, stakeholder engagement, and analytical decision-making are implied by the work described but not explicitly framed in the language of the target role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is strong. The CV uses conventional headings, reverse-chronological experience, readable text formatting, standard date ranges, and relevant searchable terms including Azure, Terraform, Azure DevOps, AKS, Kubernetes, networking, security, Windows Server, Linux, and virtual machines. It should parse well and has a high AI screening probability for Azure-focused cloud infrastructure roles. The document correctly does not claim AWS, Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, or IoT experience that is not supported by the candidate information. Adding a more explicit but truthful systems-architecture phrase would improve matching against this particular advertisement without keyword stuffing.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document strongly demonstrates hands-on infrastructure engineering and Azure cloud environment design and operation. Terraform, Azure networking, landing-zone work, AKS operations, CI/CD, virtual machines, Linux, and practical security controls are well aligned. The migration and landing-zone work also provide credible evidence of technical ownership and architecture-related work. The main candidate gaps are strong Terragrunt experience, mTLS and SSL/TLS knowledge, AWS, IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, and a backend or full-stack background, especially JVM-based development. The CV also does not provide direct evidence of agreeing interfaces with external manufacturers or bringing multiple stakeholder groups along. These are capability gaps rather than document defects and should not be solved by adding unsupported claims. The CV is a good match for the infrastructure and platform aspects of the role, but a less complete match for the secure train-to-cloud and stakeholder-heavy aspects.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT 1 — In the Professional Summary section, revise the final sentence so the existing architecture-related evidence is stated in the job advertisement’s terminology. For example, change the summary to include: "Experience includes Azure landing-zone and systems-architecture work, AKS operations, a 60-server VMware-to-Azure migration, and improving deployment frequency for internal applications." Only use this wording if "systems-architecture work" accurately reflects the candidate’s involvement in the landing-zone design and migration planning already documented.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT 2 — In the Core Skills section, change the heading "Networking and security" to "Networking, systems architecture and security" and retain the existing skills underneath it. This makes the architecture focus more discoverable to ATS and recruiters without adding unsupported technologies or experience.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT 3 — In the Cloud Engineer experience section under Havenstad Logistics, make the technical ownership of the landing-zone work slightly more explicit by changing "Developed Terraform modules for hub-spoke landing zone networking" to "Developed Terraform modules and the supporting network design for a hub-spoke Azure landing zone, including Azure Firewall, private endpoints and connectivity across subscriptions." This is supported by the documented Azure landing-zone networking project and should only be used if the candidate was responsible for the supporting network design, not merely implementation.
